study type: Prospective observational study with case-control comparison
outcome: Requirement for additional therapy (blood transfusion, non-standard hypertensive therapy)
cohort: The study participants were 35 pregnant women whose maternal serum samples were analyzed at specific gestational ages and divided into subgroups based on preeclampsia occurrence at delivery, with a matched control group.
finding: The sFLT-1/PlGF ratio was significantly higher in the preterm delivery preeclampsia group and negatively correlated with gestational age and birth weight at delivery, indicating its potential as an indicator for preeclampsia development and severity, and as a predictive marker.
mod_finding: All preeclampsia group pregnancies ended with caesarean delivery, compared to 25% in the control group.
cross-section timing: Maternal serum samples were analyzed at 24 1/7 to 28 0/7 weeks and 28 1/7 to 32 0/7 weeks of gestation.
birth_weight: Infant birth weight was measured as an outcome and found to be lower in the preterm delivery group.
gest_age: Gestational age was used for timing of serum sample collection (24-32 weeks), to define subgroups (preterm <=37 weeks, term 37-42 weeks), and lower gestational age at delivery was an outcome.
